title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An Avride autonomous vehicle struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood in Austin, Texas. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and did not slow down or stop after the collision, according to resident reports. It is not established whether the vehicle's perception system failed to detect the duck, whether its decision-making system chose not to brake, or what technical factors contributed to the outcome.

This incident shows a deployed autonomous system encountering an object in its path during normal operation and failing to avoid it. The failure occurred in a residential area where the vehicle was in active autonomous control with no human operator to intervene. Catching this would have required either better animal detection capabilities in the perception system, or decision logic that prioritizes braking for small animals in neighborhood settings, or human monitoring with the ability to take control.

It is not established whether similar incidents have occurred with other autonomous vehicle operators in the area, or what safety standards apply to animal strikes by self-driving cars.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, triggering significant community backlash. A resident reported on social media that the self-driving car did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant and was familiar to neighbors. Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode during the incident and disputed a claim that it failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it made complete stops at all relevant intersections.

In response to the incident, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by restricting autonomous vehicles from certain streets around the lake where the accident occurred. The company is now evaluating technological improvements to prevent similar situations, including running controlled simulation experiments. Meanwhile, concerned residents have retrieved the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, also operate in Austin, though this incident has raised questions in the community about whether self-driving cars should be operating in residential areas.
